title: The AR-RC13 lockstep test pins a duplicated literal, not the module's actual terminal_statuses const — const↔shared-fn drift is uncaught
evidence:
server/src/application/application_detail_handler.gleam:1286: `const terminal_statuses: List(String) = [` (private const, drives build_attempt_log terminal_entries at :1454).
server/test/application/application_detail_handler_test.gleam:594-603:
```
  let terminal = [
    "form_completed",
    "manual_recorded",
    "unreachable",
    "refused",
    "objected",
    "partial",
    "failed",
    "completed",
  ]
```
architecture-reference-checking-v1-2026-07-29.md:135: `lockstep unit test pins the timeline's DB-string `terminal_statuses` list to the shared`
detail: The test checks the shared fn against its own hardcoded copy; it never reads the module const (Gleam consts are private). Adding a status to terminal_statuses alone fails nothing — the exact mirror-drift class AR-RC13 names.
recommended_fix: Expose the const via a pub fn and iterate the REAL list both directions: every const entry terminal per shared fn, and every shared-terminal variant present in the const.

title: lint_refcheck_hooks.py false-positives on hook-gated construction nested inside a non-hook case (e.g. a status sub-case within a hooks case)
detail: The upward scan treats any shallower non-hook `case` opener as a disconnect, so a legitimate future refactor (status sub-menu inside a hooks case — the inverse of today's overflow_actions nesting) fails CI and forces restructuring.
recommended_fix: Track hook-case open/close pairs explicitly (depth counter) instead of bailing on the first shallower `case`; at minimum, document the nesting constraint in the lint's docstring.

title: The hooks lint is bypassable by multiline list construction — gleam format preserves the escaping shape
evidence:
scripts/lint_refcheck_hooks.py:76-77:
```
            marker = action + "]"
            if marker not in line:
                continue
```
Empirically verified: `case call.status { Unreachable -> [\n      RefcheckTakeOver,\n      RefcheckSubstitute,\n    ] ... }` passes the lint (marker `RefcheckSubstitute]` never lands on one line); `gleam format` leaves that multiline trailing-comma list unchanged, and the format-check gate is satisfied.
detail: The guard is formatting-dependent: a re-derived status menu written multiline ships past lint and format-check. The two distinguishing panel tests still cover the historical statuses, so this is a deterrent gap, not a live hole.
recommended_fix: Scan for the action identifier in construction position regardless of line breaks (track list-context across lines), or add a matching panel test per new status arm.

title: Em-dash enforcement for copy.gleam rests on hand-maintained test lists — the lint exempts the module wholesale
evidence:
scripts/lint_em_dash.py:33: `CLIENT_EXCLUDE = {"client/src/copy.gleam"}`
client/test/copy_test.gleam:310: `fn refcheck_action_strings() -> List(String) {` and :371: `fn refcheck_fn_built_labels() -> List(String) {` — both manually enumerated const/fn lists; `no_em_dash_test` only reaches toast/page arms automatically (`for_each_copy`).
detail: The lint scans all client render modules except copy.gleam; inside copy.gleam, only manually listed strings are checked. A new implementer-authored const or fn-built label with an em-dash ships unless its author remembers to list it.
recommended_fix: Either narrow the exemption (scan copy.gleam, whitelist the spec-verbatim strings) or generate the scan lists from the copy module so new strings are covered by default.

title: outcome_from_string_optional is a third hand-copied outcome table with no full lockstep pin against encode_outcome
detail: The file now holds three copies of the string↔outcome mapping. A new outcome added to encode_outcome but missed in the optional fn silently encodes as absent (null) on the wire — failure direction is safe, but undetected.
recommended_fix: Extend every_outcome_round_trips_test with `outcome_from_string_optional(encode_outcome(o)) == Some(o)` for all outcomes, or build both fns from one internal mapping.
